_note: The four conditions in scope. `summary` and `severityGuidance` are neutral editorial text. `symptoms` weights are editorial. `remedies` links (which remedy, which severity band) are INHERITED FROM THE LEGACY DATASET and are not clinically validated — see each link's provenance. `whenToSeeProfessional` / `generalPrecautions` are sourced from the cited NHS pages.

conditions.name: Gastritis
conditions.summary: Irritation or inflammation of the stomach lining, often felt as burning or gnawing discomfort in the upper abdomen, indigestion, nausea, or feeling full quickly. It can be short-lived or ongoing.

severityGuidance.mild: Occasional discomfort that settles on its own and does not stop you eating or sleeping.
severityGuidance.moderate: Frequent or daily discomfort that affects appetite, meals, or sleep.
severityGuidance.severe: Constant or intense pain, repeated vomiting, or any sign of bleeding — this needs medical assessment, not a home remedy.

remedies.note: Paired with higher-severity gastritis in the legacy data.

generalPrecautions.value: Persistent indigestion (lasting three weeks or more) should be reviewed by a doctor rather than managed only at home.

whenToSeeProfessional.value: See a doctor if indigestion keeps coming back, does not improve, is painful, or starts alongside weight loss, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, or feeling full very quickly.
Get emergency help for vomit that is bright red or looks like ground coffee, stools that are black and tarry, or severe pain that started suddenly.

verification.summary: Symptom associations and severity descriptions are editorial. Professional-care guidance is sourced from NHS. Remedy links are inherited from the legacy dataset and not clinically validated.

conditions.name: Diarrhea
conditions.summary: Passing loose or watery stools more often than usual, sometimes with cramps, urgency, or nausea. Most short episodes settle within a few days; the main risk is losing too much fluid.

severityGuidance.mild: A few loose stools, still able to eat and drink normally, no marked thirst.
severityGuidance.moderate: Frequent loose stools with cramps, needing effort to keep fluids up.
severityGuidance.severe: Unable to keep fluids down, very little urine, blood in the stool, or lasting more than a week — seek medical care.

remedies.note: The most frequently paired remedy for moderate diarrhea in the legacy data.
Legacy pairing; haritaki is more usually described as a bowel regulator, so this association warrants review.
Sitopaladi churna is classically a respiratory formulation; this diarrhea pairing looks like a legacy-data artefact and needs review.

generalPrecautions.value: The priority in any diarrhoea is fluids. Small, frequent sips of water or an oral rehydration solution matter more than any specific remedy.

whenToSeeProfessional.value: Contact a doctor if there is blood in the stool, if diarrhoea lasts more than 7 days or vomiting more than 2 days, or if you cannot keep fluids down or are passing very little urine.
Get emergency help for a stiff neck with sensitivity to light, a sudden severe headache or tummy ache, or pale, blotchy or blue-tinged skin.

verification.summary: Symptom associations and severity descriptions are editorial. Rehydration and professional-care guidance is sourced from NHS. Remedy links are inherited from the legacy dataset; several look like data artefacts and are flagged for review.

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.summary: A headache disorder, usually felt as a moderate-to-severe throbbing pain often on one side of the head, frequently with nausea and sensitivity to light or sound, and sometimes preceded by visual disturbance (aura).

severityGuidance.mild: A headache you can work through, easing with rest or the usual over-the-counter painkiller.
severityGuidance.moderate: A headache that disrupts your day and makes normal activity difficult.
severityGuidance.severe: A headache that is disabling, unusually intense, unusually long, or different from your normal pattern — this warrants medical review.

remedies.note: Ginger has some sourced evidence for migraine-associated nausea (see remedy record).
Shankha prakshalana is an intensive cleansing procedure, not a remedy to self-administer; retained for traceability only.

generalPrecautions.value: A headache that is new, suddenly different from your usual pattern, or steadily worsening over days to weeks should be assessed rather than self-treated.

whenToSeeProfessional.value: See a doctor urgently if a migraine lasts longer than 72 hours, if aura symptoms last more than an hour, or if you are pregnant or recently gave birth.

Call emergency services for a sudden extremely painful headache, problems speaking or remembering, vision loss, drowsiness or confusion, a seizure, weakness on one side of the body or face, or a headache after a recent head injury.

conditions.name: Arthritis
conditions.summary: An umbrella term for joint pain, stiffness, and sometimes swelling or reduced movement. Many different conditions cause it, and management depends on which one.

severityGuidance.mild: Occasional aches or stiffness that do not limit everyday activity.
severityGuidance.moderate: Daily pain or stiffness that makes some tasks harder.
severityGuidance.severe: Pain that is constant or disabling, a hot or visibly swollen joint, or pain with fever — this needs medical assessment.

remedies.note: Both components (boswellia, turmeric/curcumin) have some sourced evidence for joint symptoms — see remedy record.
Ginger has some sourced evidence for osteoarthritis symptoms — see remedy record.

generalPrecautions.value: Because many different conditions cause arthritis, a diagnosis matters — the right management for one type can be wrong for another.

whenToSeeProfessional.value: See a doctor if joint pain, swelling, or stiffness does not settle within a few days, or if painkillers are not helping.
Seek urgent care for sudden severe pain and swelling in a single joint, a joint that is hot or red, or joint pain alongside fever, a rash, eye inflammation, or urinary symptoms.
